title: Diraq Finalizes $38 Million CHIPS R&D Award with U.S. Department of Commerce for Silicon Spin Quantum Chips - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Silicon spin-qubit developer Diraq has finalized a funding agreement of up to $38 million with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office under the CHIPS and Science Act, converting a Letter of Intent announced in May 2026 into a definitive award. The funding will accelerate U.S.-based fabrication, testing, and research infrastructure for Diraq’s CMOS-compatible silicon quantum processors, targeting key scaling bottlenecks including scalable Quantum Logic Units (QLUs), novel qubit arrays, and global qubit control.

The only silicon spin-qubit company selected in this CHIPS R&D round, Diraq is pairing its Australian scientific operations with expanded U.S. facilities in Palo Alto, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Albuquerque. Designed to operate within a compact four-rack data center footprint, the company’s roadmap targets 150,000 physical qubits supporting up to 1,000 logical qubits by 2029, scaling to more than two million physical qubits and over 10,000 logical qubits by 2031, following its advancement to Stage C of DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and a commercial data-center deployment with Equinix.

Read Diraq’s announcement here and view the U.S. Department of Commerce and NIST release here. Related QCR coverage includes our earlier report on the Department of Commerce’s $2 billion CHIPS quantum Letters of Intent here.
